pull.title: Desktop shell: winget manifest, and repin path A to 6.45.2 (S8)
pull.body:
Spec S8, plus the pin move that has to go with it. Version **6.45.3** (PATCH).

## 1. The repin: path A now fetches the 6.45.2 shell

`DESKTOP_SHELL_RELEASE_TAG` moves `v6.43.0` → `v6.45.2`, with all four archive
digests replaced from that release's own `SHA256SUMS-desktop-shell.txt`
(`gh release download v6.45.2 -p SHA256SUMS-desktop-shell.txt`), never typed by hand:

| target | asset | old | new |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `linux/x86_64` | `MyClaudeCode-linux-x86_64.tar.gz` | `ec4f92d6…a08a55f` | `46040b4b…6eebae0` |
| `darwin/x86_64` | `MyClaudeCode-macos-x86_64.tar.gz` | `41d059d3…d1b7ff96` | `c0ca0e56…045373ee` |
| `darwin/aarch64` | `MyClaudeCode-macos-aarch64.tar.gz` | `cfc66ea6…242d24183` | `f5a694a6…45dd44818` |
| `win32/x86_64` | `MyClaudeCode-windows-x86_64.zip` | `3a159d24…fa92436e` | `f71368ef…5c74f7f76` |

**A repin can no longer drift.** That release's checksum file is vendored at
`tests/fixtures/desktop_shell/v6.45.2/`, and `test_desktop_shell_pin.py` compares
the in-source table against it on every run. The network-gated test already made
this comparison against the live release, but it is opt-in and therefore silent
on exactly the pull request where a mistyped digest is cheap to catch. The
fixture directory is named for the pinned tag, so a repin that forgets to vendor
fails on a missing directory rather than passing against the previous release's
digests. `.gitattributes` checks the directory out with `-text` so the
comparison is against bytes and not against a re-encoded copy of itself.

**The Linux tarball grew members (#279) and the extraction rule tolerates it.**
The v6.45.2 archive carries `install-desktop.sh`, a `.desktop` entry and four
icons beside the binary. Path A's rule was never "one member" — it is "exactly
one member whose base name is `MyClaudeCode`, and no links". That is now asserted
against the **released** archive's real member list: `tar -tzvf` is vendored as a
fixture (the listing, not the 4.6 MB tarball), parsed, replayed into an in-memory
tar of the same shape, and run through the real `_extract_binary`.

**Path A proved end to end on Windows.** Scratch `MCC_CONFIG_DIR`,
`MCC_DESKTOP_SHELL_DIR`, `MCC_DESKTOP_SKIP_AUTOSTART=1`, `PORT=8199`
`HOST=127.0.0.1`; port 8082 checked first and left alone (still PID 48392
throughout). `mcc-desktop` fetched `MyClaudeCode-windows-x86_64.zip`, verified it
against the pin *and* the published sums file, installed it into the scratch
directory and wrote a receipt naming `v6.45.2` and `f71368ef…`; the window opened
on the dashboard against a scratch server on 8199 (screenshot captured with
`PrintWindow`, checked by eye — Get Started renders, footer shows the scratch
`.env`). Everything was stopped by exact PID.

## 2. The winget manifest

`desktop-shell/installer/winget/` — three files at **manifest schema 1.28.0**
(the newest published in `microsoft/winget-pkgs` `doc/manifest/schema/`; not
guessed) for `FiredMosquito831.MyClaudeCode` 6.45.2:

- `Architecture: x64`, `InstallerType: inno`, `Scope: user`, the v6.45.2
  `MyClaudeCode-Setup-windows-x86_64.exe` URL and its published SHA-256;
- `AppsAndFeaturesEntries` with `ProductCode: '{5FC8D5C3-…}_is1'` — the `.iss`
  `AppId` with `_is1`, read out of the `.iss` rather than repeated — plus the
  `DisplayName`, `DisplayVersion` and `Publisher` Inno actually writes;
- **no `InstallerSwitches`**: `inno` already means winget supplies
  `/SP- /VERYSILENT /SUPPRESSMSGBOXES /NORESTART`
  (`winget-cli`'s `GetDefaultKnownSwitches`), and its docs ask you not to
  duplicate it;
- **no `Commands`**: the installer deliberately puts nothing on `PATH`.

**Publisher segment = the GitHub owner.** The community repository asks for "the
name of the company that publishes the tool"; there is no company, and its own
convention for that case is the account name (`sharkdp.bat`,
`ajeetdsouza.zoxide`). It is also the only half of the identifier a user could
guess from the URL they downloaded from. This deliberately differs from
`AppsAndFeaturesEntries.Publisher` (`My Claude Code`), which is not a display
name but the string winget reads back out of the registry.

**Rendered, not written.** `render.py` (stdlib only) reads the six values that
live elsewhere and would go stale silently — the `AppId`, the three Apps &
Features strings, `pyproject.toml`'s licence, and the digest from the release's
checksum file — and prints the manifests. `tests/scripts/test_winget_manifest.py`
asserts that rendering v6.45.2 reproduces the committed files byte for byte, so
the checked-in copies are safe to read and to copy into a submission, and a
changed `AppId` is a red test rather than a package winget quietly stops
recognising.

```
uv run --offline python desktop-shell/installer/winget/render.py v6.45.2
```

## 3. Validation and the install/uninstall proof

Windows 11 26100, winget **v1.29.290**.

```
> winget validate --manifest desktop-shell\installer\winget\6.45.2
Manifest validation succeeded.
```

`winget install --manifest` is **blocked on this machine** by the
`LocalManifestFiles` admin policy, and `winget settings --enable LocalManifestFiles`
refuses without elevation (exit 25; no UAC prompt was raised and nothing was
escalated). So the install was done with the exact command winget would have run:
the release asset, downloaded and hash-checked against the manifest's
`InstallerSha256`, with winget-cli's own inno switch set.

| step | result |
| --- | --- |
| digest of the downloaded asset | `FB78D850…0DBFF8F` — equals the manifest's `InstallerSha256` |
| `/SP- /VERYSILENT /SUPPRESSMSGBOXES /NORESTART` | exit **0**, no prompt, no elevation |
| `HKCU\…\Uninstall\{5FC8D5C3-…}_is1` | `DisplayName: My Claude Code (desktop app)`, `DisplayVersion: 6.45.2`, `Publisher: My Claude Code` — all three as declared |
| `winget list --name "My Claude Code"` | id `ARP\User\X64\{5FC8D5C3-33F7-4366-AD8D-C844D21BC089}_is1` — i.e. `Scope: user` + `Architecture: x64` + the manifest's `ProductCode`, character for character |
| `winget list --id FiredMosquito831.MyClaudeCode` | *no package found* — correct, and the whole point: that identifier does not exist in any source until the submission is merged |
| the installed exe, launched against a `server_presence: foreign` stub | window up, port-conflict page, **started nothing**, exited on its exact PID (`smoke/windows.ps1` passed) |
| silent uninstall via the registered `QuietUninstallString` | exit **0**; program dir, Start Menu shortcut and ARP key all gone |

Snapshot diff, taken before the install and again after the uninstall:

```
hkcu-uninstall.txt        : identical (35 entries)
hkcu-run.txt              : identical (16 entries)
start-menu.txt            : identical (556 entries)
localappdata-programs.txt : identical (138030 entries)
local-bin.txt             : identical (50 entries)
```

Empty, all five. The real `~/.local/bin` (which holds the live `mcc-server`
shim), the real HKCU `Run` value and the live server on 8082 were untouched.

## 4. Submission: prepared, deliberately not made

Nothing has been forked, branched, pushed or opened under
`microsoft/winget-pkgs`. Claiming a package identifier in a Microsoft-run index
is permanent and awkward to undo, so it is the maintainer's call.

`desktop-shell/installer/winget/SUBMIT.md` has the destination path
(`manifests/f/FiredMosquito831/MyClaudeCode/6.45.2/`), both routes
(`wingetcreate`/`komac` and a manual fork), the PR title and body ready to paste,
and the moderator checklist — silent install, working uninstall, `ProductCode`
matching Apps & Features — with the evidence for each already gathered above.

## 5. Docs

- README and `docs/USAGE.md`: the Windows row and the Path B section gain
  `winget install FiredMosquito831.MyClaudeCode`, explicitly gated on "once the
  manifest is accepted", with a pointer to `SUBMIT.md` so the gate is honest.
- `docs/RELEASE-CHECKLIST.md` §8 gains the vendor-the-fixture step (and the
  tarball-listing refresh) and the scratch path-A proof; a new §9 covers the
  winget render for future releases.
- `desktop-shell/README.md` gains a **winget** section: why it is rendered, the
  three deliberate absences, and the publisher-segment reasoning.

## 6. Checks

`ruff format --check`, `ruff check`, `ty check` clean. **9706 passed, 56 skipped**
(the 39 new tests also pass under `-n0`). No `# type: ignore`. Contracts green,
including docs drift, uninstaller parity and the single-sourced config dir.

commit.message:
feat(desktop): winget manifest, and repin path A to the 6.45.2 shell

Two things that belong in one release, because the winget manifest describes
the 6.45.2 installer and the pin should not still be naming 6.43.0 when it does.

**The repin.** `DESKTOP_SHELL_RELEASE_TAG` moves to `v6.45.2` with all four
archive digests, read out of that release's own `SHA256SUMS-desktop-shell.txt`
and not typed. That file is now *vendored* under `tests/fixtures/desktop_shell/`
and `test_desktop_shell_pin.py` compares the in-source table against it on every
run. The network-gated check already proved the pin against the live release,
but it is opt-in and therefore silent on exactly the pull request where a
mistyped digest is cheap to catch; the fixture makes it ordinary CI, and makes
the repin reviewable, because the table and the file it came from change in the
same commit. `.gitattributes` checks that directory out byte-for-byte, so the
comparison cannot degrade into comparing a copy of itself.

The v6.45.2 Linux tarball also carries `install-desktop.sh`, a `.desktop` entry
and four icons (#279). Path A's rule was never "one member" -- it is "exactly
one member named `MyClaudeCode`, and no links" -- and that is now asserted
against the *released* archive's real member list, vendored as a `tar -tzvf`
listing and replayed through the real extractor. Path A was proved end to end on
Windows against a scratch config dir, shell dir and port: it fetched the 6.45.2
zip, verified it against both sources, wrote a receipt naming the new tag, and
rendered the dashboard.

**The winget manifest** (spec S8) lives in `desktop-shell/installer/winget/`:
three files at schema 1.28.0 for `FiredMosquito831.MyClaudeCode` 6.45.2,
`InstallerType: inno`, `Scope: user`, and an `AppsAndFeaturesEntries` whose
`ProductCode` is the installer's fixed `AppId` with `_is1`. There is no
`InstallerSwitches` block, because `inno` already means winget supplies
`/SP- /VERYSILENT /SUPPRESSMSGBOXES /NORESTART`, and no `Commands`, because the
installer deliberately puts nothing on PATH.

They are rendered by `render.py` rather than written, because six of their
values live elsewhere in this repo and go stale silently -- the `AppId`, the
three Apps & Features strings, the licence and the published digest. A test
asserts that rendering 6.45.2 reproduces the committed bytes, so the checked-in
copies are safe to read and to submit, and a changed `AppId` is a red test
rather than a package winget quietly stops recognising.

Verified on Windows 11 26100 with winget v1.29.290: `winget validate` passes;
the real release asset installs with winget's own inno switch set (exit 0, no
prompt, no elevation); the Apps & Features entry matches all four declared
fields; `winget list` reports the installed package as
`ARP\User\X64\{5FC8D5C3-...}_is1`, which is `Scope` + `Architecture` +
`ProductCode` exactly; the registered `QuietUninstallString` removes it; and
`HKCU\...\Uninstall`, `HKCU\...\Run`, both Start Menu trees,
`%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs` and `~/.local/bin` diff empty before and after.

`winget install --manifest` itself is blocked on this machine by the
`LocalManifestFiles` admin policy, which cannot be enabled without elevation;
the proof above runs the installer with the exact switch set winget-cli's
`GetDefaultKnownSwitches` supplies for `inno`, which is the same command.

**Nothing has been submitted to `microsoft/winget-pkgs`**, and nothing there has
been forked or opened. Claiming a package identifier in a Microsoft-run index is
the maintainer's call; `SUBMIT.md` carries the exact steps, the pull-request text
ready to paste, and the moderator checklist with the evidence for each item
already gathered.
